analysis: Both units are base-side excerpts of fixtures/prompt-contract/v1/production_vectors.json (base lines 9140-10756). They contain test vectors only: chat/completions/messages/responses request bodies, provider bodies, template inputs, prompt-contract plans and token IDs for the qwen "unicode" case and gemma-4-26b cases. The patch excerpt shows the PR changes only the fixtures: it adds additional_context.enable_thinking=false to a Qwen-family case, and changes prompt_token_count, block boundaries/chain hashes and token IDs. It touches no executable code, key handling, attestation, authorization, WebSocket, encryption or billing logic. The fixture content has no secrets; the values are synthetic test strings and public token IDs. Threat-model relevance is indirect: the prompt-contract and cache-routing behaviour touches T-041 (cross-tenant prefix-cache and TTFT oracle). Changed chain hashes and block boundaries should be consumed consistently by the Go coordinator and the Swift provider. The fixture-consuming code and the production prompt-contract/cache-key implementation were not supplied, so I cannot confirm that the new vectors match the runtime. The fixtures also do not weaken any existing control. The patch excerpt is truncated and the provided units are base side, so head-side vectors were not directly reviewed. I found no concrete security regression from the supplied evidence. Integration should confirm that the prompt_contract_id, chain-hash derivation and enable_thinking template handling are validated identically by coordinator and provider code, and that cache scope isolation (scope_id) is unchanged.
